opencode2-compat in wave 1 contradicts ceo-any-cli (francovp targets OpenCode 1.x) and upstream #311 local models (OpenCode 1 schema plus --model). Nobody has decided whether OpenCode 1 stays supported. Gate it on detected version (Calel33's cached `opencode --version`) or move it out of wave 1. The OpenCode 2 claims were not verified against a real binary.

ws-origin-check and loopback-request-boundary overlap and are both in wave 1. Merge them into one middleware. loopback-request-boundary is not a quick win: as written its hard-coded loopback allowlist breaks --host, pocket mode over LAN/Tailscale and the preview gateway. Neither covers upstream #310's preview pages, which are served same-origin and so pass every Origin check.

Ordering: the request boundary must land before any new mutating route (manager-refinement-after-qa, decision room, manager-mcp-gateway, chat attachments, the file reveal text route). Several of those add merge/close/approve endpoints that a cross-site page can currently POST to.

Eight wave 1 items edit mergeGate.ts mergeStep and swarm.ts advanceMerge/mergePull: fail-closed-merge-gate, branch-update-requeues-qa, paul-merge-gate-findings, tubadog-merge-holds, tubadog-routine-only-automerge, tubadog-qa-skip-held-drafts, kk-draft-pr-ready, manager-refinement-after-qa. Treated as independent quick wins they produce a conflict storm and inconsistent gate semantics. Give them one owner and one sequence: gate core, SHA-requeue rule (add the missing hand-merge-requeue-on-head-move), holds, routine-only, held-draft skip, draft-ready, refinement.

fail-closed-merge-gate is M and changes behaviour, not a quick win. Unchanged, it never merges repos without CI, refuses UNSTABLE/HAS_HOOKS, and removes the manager's manual merge override. It needs an explicit checks:'none' policy (ADR-011) and an audited override (FR-035) before it ships.

kk-draft-pr-ready auto-undrafts QA-passed drafts and feeds them to auto-merge. Next to tubadog's swarm:hold drafts and needs-input drafts, that removes the human 'not ready' signal unless it checks holds first, and fail-closed-merge-gate refuses drafts in the same mergeStep. Make it per-floor opt-in and order it after holds.

tubadog-routine-only-automerge loads routineOnly ?? true. Existing auto-merge floors would start holding dependency, CI and large PRs after the import. Default it OFF (ADR-009, FR-005: no new gates without opt-in). Its glob heuristics ('auth', '*secret*') over-match.

eddie-floor-budgets is in wave 1, but cost telemetry (eddie-cost-telemetry) is in wave 2. Budgets count only reported Claude cost, so on Codex/OpenCode floors they never trigger. They are also lifetime-only with no reset. Either move it after telemetry or ship it with a visible 'cost unknown for this CLI' state (NFR-010).

CEO panel and settings need supermini-world-decoupling (65 files, 2180 lines, code moved out of store.ts and sfx.ts, which churn at 52 and 25 commits per month upstream) and supermini-settings-sections-split (1350 lines out of ManagerConsole). It also needs the extra copyright line in LICENSE and a pickMode flip so 3D stays the default. This is a structural refactor, not a quick win.

copilot-cli-agent is not low risk despite its 'cherry-pick' label. Its flags and hook payloads are unverifiable, the model ids look made up, it has no cost parser, and it adds a fourth CLI to every per-CLI table (limits, catalog, QA pairing, telemetry) before the RFC's per-CLI capability matrix exists. kk-trust-prompt-fixes has two more complete siblings (faustosip-trust-prompt-fix and folder-trust-under-older-screens, both upstream closed PR #286). The adopted-CLI and hook-review cases matter more once ceo-any-cli reuses the CEO terminal across CLIs. Plan the #286 follow-up instead of treating trust prompts as done.

Wave 2 ports ideas-prd-review-publication (XL, about 1000 lines of role-based swarm.ts glue) and tubadog-floor-lead (+500 lines in swarm.ts) into Swarm. The RFC's executive decision is a workflow layer built next to swarm.ts, not inside it. Lift their pure modules as seeds for WF-002 and WF-010..WF-012 instead of replaying the glue.

tubadog-floor-lead should not be imported as is. It adds an AgentRole 'lead' (against upstream #288's role removal and ADR-002's 'no role enum explosion'), runs one standing paid Claude session per floor by default, hard-codes model ids, and takes triage away from the CEO. Keep only the scoped-tool pattern for WF-006. eddie-takes-roles has the same problem.

Wave 2 carries three incompatible telemetry stores: multi-provider-ai-usage (unbounded array in state.json, findIndex on every insert, no demo fake), eddie-cost-telemetry, and run-history-telemetry. Pick one observation schema and one rotated store, shaped for WF-004/WF-013, before porting any of them.

per-cli-session-limits is in wave 2 without claude-only-usage-brakes, although the audit says to port them as one unit. It also overlaps session-slot-reservation and droidsembly's QuotaGate on the same slotsFull/pacing code. Decide the combined design once.

manager-mcp-gateway gives one bearer token full manager power, including merge and approval. That lets an external agent approve its own spec or PR, which contradicts FR-025 and ADR-008 (approvers cannot self-attest). Exclude approval and merge tools, or record a distinct non-human principal, and land it only after the request boundary.

qa-security-review-escalation depends on repo-managed-skills-specialisms (it executes the vendored Cloudflare security-audit skill and its .cjs validators), so the skills must come first. Its label-based waiver lets anyone with write access skip the security review, against FR-032 and ADR-005. Drop the waiver.

qa-findings-and-evidence lets QA push applied suggestions, which breaks the office rule that QA leaves GitHub alone. Its Codex-connector thread triage assumes a specific third-party bot. Strip both and keep the SHA-pinned outcomes and stable finding IDs.

eddie-qa-pairing depends on shared/cli.ts resolveCli from eddie-ceo-any-cli, which is not being imported. Re-derive runtimeCli on top of francovp's ceo-any-cli and upstream's current sessionRuntime (box hosts).

tubadog-decision-room in wave 2 without first generalizing upstream's existing HireRequestView/PocketApprovals (the RFC gap asks for exactly that) would give the office several approval inboxes: Pocket approvals, decision room, the ideas approval card, the supermini CEO panel and Kanban 'request changes'. Decide on one approval-request model before porting.

tubadog-decision-briefs adds DECISIONS_RULE and the brief template to every build/fix prompt, a cost paid on every session per CLAUDE.md, and decides merges with the regex recommendsMerge(). Make the brief a typed artifact with an enum recommendation. Never take tubadog-decision-clock's default action, which auto-merges held auth/migration PRs after 48 h.

read-only-analysis-task is woven into droidsembly's OpenCode V2 commit 8adf85b and overlaps Saredigital's analysis-tasks-reports. Porting it as a new swarm task type now makes throwaway work if WF-008 (ai.task executor) follows. Port it directly as that executor.

global-scheduler-pause has two siblings that were not considered (close-office, box-daily-operations' cloud pause). Ship one persisted pause flag, re-implemented on upstream's scheduler with localloop's 353-line test as the spec, because WF-007 needs exactly one.

Neither wave builds any part of the RFC core (WF-001..WF-009). Almost everything imported improves the legacy swarm.ts pipeline that the RFC plans to wrap as one cubefarm.development stage (ADR-007, open). Settle ADR-007 before wave 2, or wave 2 grows the 5.5k-line hotspot the RFC is trying to avoid.

No fork-maintenance item is shortlisted (eddie-upstream-drift-check, kk-fork-safety-guide), although the fork has no upstream remote and every wave adds drift in swarm.ts, cliRunner.ts and ManagerConsole.
